test_cases.summary:
Verify system prevents saving session when name is empty
when the user is on Create Session form
test_cases.description:
Feature: Session Name Mandatory – Empty Block

Scenario: Verify system prevents saving session when name is empty

Given the user is on Create Session form
When the user leaves Session Name field empty
And clicks Save/Create
Then the system should block creation
And show toast message “Name is required”
test_cases.acceptance:
The system should block creation
The behavior should be validated when the user leaves Session Name field empty.

test_cases.summary:
Verify missing session name message is clear and descriptive
when the user clicks Save without entering Session Name
test_cases.description:

Scenario: Verify missing session name message is clear and descriptive

Given the user clicks Save without entering Session Name
When validation fails
Then the toast message should clearly describe the missing Name field
And should not show technical error codes
test_cases.acceptance:
The toast message should clearly describe the missing Name field
The behavior should be validated when validation fails.

test_cases.acceptance:
The toast message should clearly mention the allowed maximum length
The behavior should be validated when Save is clicked.

test_cases.summary:

test_cases.summary:
Verify system prevents creating session with duplicate name
when a session already exists with Name "SESSION_ALPHA"
test_cases.description:
Feature: Session Name Uniqueness – Duplicate Block

Scenario: Verify system prevents creating session with duplicate name

Given a session already exists with Name “SESSION_ALPHA”
When the user enters Session Name as “SESSION_ALPHA” again
And clicks Save/Create
Then the system should block creation
And show toast message “A session with the name “SESSION_ALPHA” already exists. Please choose a different name.”
test_cases.acceptance:
The system should block creation
The behavior should be validated when the user enters Session Name as "SESSION_ALPHA" again.

test_cases.summary:
Verify duplicate session message includes the entered session name
when the user enters a session name that already exists
test_cases.description:
Feature: Session Name Uniqueness – Message Contains Entered Name

Given the user enters a session name that already exists
When Save is clicked
Then the toast message should include the session name entered by the user
And should not show technical database errors
test_cases.acceptance:
The toast message should include the session name entered by the user
The behavior should be validated when Save is clicked.

test_cases.summary:
Verify system prevents saving session when any approval level has no user selected
when the user configured Approval Levels (L1, L2...)
test_cases.description:
Feature: Approval Level Population – Block Empty Level User List

Scenario: Verify system prevents saving session when any approval level has no user selected

Given the user configured Approval Levels (L1, L2...)
When the user leaves at least one approval level without selecting any users
And clicks Save/Create Session
Then the system should block submission
And show toast message “Each approval level must have at least one user selected”
test_cases.acceptance:
The system should block submission
The behavior should be validated when the user leaves at least one approval level without selecting any users.

test_cases.summary:
Verify approval level error message clearly explains what is missing
when the user attempts to save session with empty approval level users
test_cases.description:
Feature: Approval Level Population – Message Clarity

Scenario: Verify approval level error message clearly explains what is missing

Given the user attempts to save session with empty approval level users
When validation fails
Then the toast message should clearly state that each level requires at least one user
And should not show technical error codes
test_cases.acceptance:
The toast message should clearly state that each level requires at least one user
The behavior should be validated when validation fails.

test_cases.summary:
Verify system prevents adding more than 5 approval levels
when the user is configuring approval levels during session creation
test_cases.description:
Feature: Approval Level Limit – Restrict to Maximum 5 Levels

Scenario: Verify system prevents adding more than 5 approval levels

Given the user is configuring approval levels during session creation
When the user adds 5 approval levels successfully
And tries to add the 6th level using Add Level button
Then the system should prevent adding the 6th level
And show toast message “Maximum of 5 approval levels allowed”
test_cases.acceptance:
The system should prevent adding the 6th level
The behavior should be validated when the user adds 5 approval levels successfully.

test_cases.summary:
Verify Add Level button becomes disabled after reaching 5 levels
when the user has configured 5 approval levels
test_cases.description:
Feature: Approval Level Limit – Add Level Button Disabled at 5

Scenario: Verify Add Level button becomes disabled after reaching 5 levels

Given the user has configured 5 approval levels
When the user views the Add Level button
Then the Add Level button should be disabled or inactive
And should not allow adding additional levels
test_cases.acceptance:
The Add Level button should be disabled or inactive
The behavior should be validated when the user views the Add Level button.

test_cases.summary:
Verify system prevents saving session without selecting assignees
when the user is on Create Session form
test_cases.description:

Then the system should block submission
And show toast message “At least one assignee is required”
test_cases.acceptance:

test_cases.summary:

when the user clicks Save without selecting any assignee
test_cases.description:
Feature: Session Assignees Mandatory – Message Clarity

Scenario: Verify missing assignee message clearly explains requirement

Given the user clicks Save without selecting any assignee
When validation fails
Then the toast message should clearly mention at least one assignee is required
And should not show technical error codes
test_cases.acceptance:
The toast message should clearly mention at least one assignee is required
The behavior should be validated when validation fails.

test_cases.summary:
Verify system prevents creating session with invalid Project ID
when the user is attempting to create a session under a project
test_cases.description:
Feature: Project ID Validity – Block Invalid Project Reference

Scenario: Verify system prevents creating session with invalid Project ID

Given the user is attempting to create a session under a project
When the linked Project ID is invalid / deleted / inactive
And the user clicks Save/Create Session
Then the system should block creation
And show toast message “Invalid reference. Please check that the related project exists and is valid.”
test_cases.acceptance:
The system should block creation
The behavior should be validated when the linked Project ID is invalid / deleted / inactive.

test_cases.summary:
Verify invalid project reference message is clear and descriptive
when the user attempts to save session with invalid project link
test_cases.description:
Feature: Project ID Validity – Error Message Detail

Scenario: Verify invalid project reference message is clear and descriptive

Given the user attempts to save session with invalid project link
When backend validation fails
Then the system should show a detailed message explaining project reference is invalid
And should not show technical error codes
test_cases.acceptance:
The system should show a detailed message explaining project reference is invalid
The behavior should be validated when backend validation fails.

test_cases.summary:
Verify system blocks session modification when session is locked
when an existing session is in Locked state
test_cases.description:
Feature: Session Lock Status – Block Edit When Locked

Scenario: Verify system blocks session modification when session is locked

Given an existing session is in Locked state
When the user tries to edit any session field
And clicks Save/Update
Then the system should block modifications
And show toast message “Session is locked”
test_cases.acceptance:
The system should block modifications
The behavior should be validated when the user tries to edit any session field.

test_cases.summary:
Verify Edit controls are disabled when session is locked
when the session is locked
test_cases.description:
Feature: Session Lock Status – UI Control Disabled

Scenario: Verify Edit controls are disabled when session is locked

Given the session is locked
When the user views session page
Then Edit button should be disabled or hidden
And user should not be able to modify fields
test_cases.acceptance:
Edit button should be disabled or hidden
The behavior should be validated when the user views session page.

test_cases.summary:
Verify system blocks save when SOP reference name or URL is missing
when the user is on Create/Edit Session page
test_cases.description:
Feature: SOP Link Integrity – Block Incomplete Reference Link

Given the user is on Create/Edit Session page
When the user adds a SOP reference with Name filled but URL empty
And clicks Save/Create Session
Then the system should block submission
And show toast message “Please ensure all Reference Names and Links are filled.”
test_cases.acceptance:
The system should block submission
The behavior should be validated when the user adds a SOP reference with Name filled but URL empty.

test_cases.summary:
Verify SOP error message is clear and descriptive
when the user attempts to save with incomplete SOP references
test_cases.description:
Feature: SOP Link Integrity – Message Clarity

Scenario: Verify SOP error message is clear and descriptive

Given the user attempts to save with incomplete SOP references
When validation fails
Then the toast message should clearly mention both Name and Link are required
And should not show technical error codes
test_cases.acceptance:
The toast message should clearly mention both Name and Link are required
The behavior should be validated when validation fails.

test_cases.summary:
Verify system blocks saving when duplicate taxonomy group names exist
when the user is configuring taxonomy groups in session creation
test_cases.description:
Feature: Taxonomy Group Uniqueness – Block Duplicate Names

Given the user is configuring taxonomy groups in session creation
When the user enters the same taxonomy group name in two rows (e.g., “Bone”)
And clicks Save/Create Session
Then the system should block submission
And show toast message “There are duplicate taxonomy group names. Please ensure all taxonomy names are unique.”
test_cases.acceptance:
The system should block submission
The behavior should be validated when the user enters the same taxonomy group name in two rows (e.g., "Bone").

test_cases.summary:
Verify taxonomy duplicate message clearly describes the issue
when the user attempts to save session with duplicate taxonomy group names
test_cases.description:
Feature: Taxonomy Group Uniqueness – Message Mentions Duplicate Issue

Scenario: Verify taxonomy duplicate message clearly describes the issue

Given the user attempts to save session with duplicate taxonomy group names
When validation fails
Then the toast message should clearly mention duplicates exist
And should not show technical error codes
test_cases.acceptance:
The toast message should clearly mention duplicates exist
The behavior should be validated when validation fails.

test_cases.summary:
Verify system blocks when same user is assigned as Assignee and Approver
when the user is on Create/Edit Session page
test_cases.description:
Feature: User Role Conflict – Block Assignee vs Approver Conflict

Scenario: Verify system blocks when same user is assigned as Assignee and Approver

Given the user is on Create/Edit Session page
When the user selects “User A” as an Assignee
And also selects “User A” in Approval Level 1
And clicks Save/Create Session
Then the system should block submission
And show toast message “User A is assigned as both Assignee and in Approval Level 1”
test_cases.acceptance:
The system should block submission
The behavior should be validated when the user selects "User A" as an Assignee.

test_cases.summary:
Verify system blocks when same user is assigned to multiple approval levels
when the user is configuring approval levels
test_cases.description:
Feature: User Role Conflict – Block Multiple Approval Level Assignment

Scenario: Verify system blocks when same user is assigned to multiple approval levels

Given the user is configuring approval levels
When the user selects “User B” in Approval Level 1
And also selects “User B” in Approval Level 2
And clicks Save/Create Session
Then the system should block submission
And show toast message “User B is assigned to multiple Approval Levels...”
test_cases.acceptance:
The system should block submission
The behavior should be validated when the user selects "User B" in Approval Level 1.

test_cases.summary:
Verify system blocks upload when filename is missing/empty
when the user is in the JSON Upload dialog
test_cases.description:

And clicks Upload/Submit
Then the system should block upload
And show toast message “Filename cannot be empty.”
test_cases.acceptance:
The system should block upload
The behavior should be validated when the user selects a file with empty filename / invalid file object name.

test_cases.summary:
Verify filename missing message is clear and descriptive
when the user attempts upload without a valid filename

And should not show technical error codes

The behavior should be validated when validation fails.

test_cases.summary:
Verify system prevents uploading JSON file when filename already exists in session
when the session already contains a file named "sample.json"
test_cases.description:
Feature: Filename Uniqueness – Block Duplicate File Upload

Scenario: Verify system prevents uploading JSON file when filename already exists in session

Given the session already contains a file named “sample.json”
When the user selects another file with filename “sample.json”
And clicks Upload
Then the system should block upload
And show toast message “A file with the name “sample.json” already exists in this session.”
test_cases.acceptance:
The system should block upload
The behavior should be validated when the user selects another file with filename "sample.json".

test_cases.summary:
Verify duplicate upload message includes the filename entered/selected
when the user uploads a file with duplicate filename
test_cases.description:
Feature: Filename Uniqueness – Message Contains Filename

Scenario: Verify duplicate upload message includes the filename entered/selected

Given the user uploads a file with duplicate filename
When backend detects duplication
Then the toast message should include the duplicate filename
And should not show technical storage errors
test_cases.acceptance:
The toast message should include the duplicate filename
The behavior should be validated when backend detects duplication.

test_cases.summary:
Verify system blocks upload for non-JSON file types
when the user is in the JSON Upload dialog
test_cases.description:
Feature: File Type Validation – Reject Non-JSON File Upload

Scenario: Verify system blocks upload for non-JSON file types

Given the user is in the JSON Upload dialog
When the user selects a file with extension “.txt” or “.csv”
And clicks Upload
Then the system should block upload
And show toast message “Invalid file type. Please upload a JSON file.”
test_cases.acceptance:
The system should block upload
The behavior should be validated when the user selects a file with extension ".txt" or ".csv".

test_cases.summary:
Verify system rejects file when extension is .json but MIME type is not application/json
when the user selects a file with ".json" extension but incorrect MIME type
test_cases.description:

Given the user selects a file with “.json” extension but incorrect MIME type
When Upload is clicked

And show toast message “Invalid file type. Please upload a JSON file.”
test_cases.acceptance:
The system should block upload
The behavior should be validated when Upload is clicked.

test_cases.summary:

when the user selects a JSON file with malformed syntax (missing braces, invalid commas, etc.)

The system should show a friendly message
The behavior should be validated when JSON.parse fails.

test_cases.summary:
Verify system blocks upload when JSON file is empty (0 KB)
when the user is in the JSON Upload dialog
test_cases.description:

Given the user is in the JSON Upload dialog
When the user selects an empty JSON file (size = 0 KB)
And clicks Upload
Then the system should reject the upload
And show toast message “The uploaded file is empty.”
test_cases.acceptance:
The system should reject the upload
The behavior should be validated when the user selects an empty JSON file (size = 0 KB).

test_cases.summary:
Verify system blocks upload when JSON parses successfully but contains no content
when the user selects a JSON file with content {}
test_cases.description:
Feature: Empty File Validation – Reject Empty JSON Object

Scenario: Verify system blocks upload when JSON parses successfully but contains no content

Given the user selects a JSON file with content {}
or empty resource structure
When the user clicks Upload
Then the system should reject processing
And show toast message “The uploaded file is empty.”
test_cases.acceptance:
The system should reject processing
The behavior should be validated when the user clicks Upload.

test_cases.summary:
Verify system blocks upload when required extracted resources are missing
when the user selects a valid JSON file
test_cases.description:

Scenario: Verify system blocks upload when required extracted resources are missing

Given the user selects a valid JSON file
When the JSON does not contain required extracted resource keys/array
And clicks Upload
Then the system should reject processing
And show toast message “The uploaded file does not contain valid extracted resources.”
test_cases.acceptance:
The system should reject processing
The behavior should be validated when the JSON does not contain required extracted resource keys/array.

test_cases.summary:
Verify extracted resources error message is detailed and user-friendly
when the user uploads JSON without required extracted resources
test_cases.description:
Feature: Extracted Resources Validation – Message Clarity

Scenario: Verify extracted resources error message is detailed and user-friendly

Given the user uploads JSON without required extracted resources
When validation fails

And should not show technical schema errors
test_cases.acceptance:

The behavior should be validated when validation fails.

test_cases.summary:
Verify system shows error toast when storage upload fails
when the user selects a valid JSON file for upload
test_cases.description:
Feature: Storage Upload Failure – Handle Network/Permission Error

Scenario: Verify system shows error toast when storage upload fails

Given the user selects a valid JSON file for upload
When the storage upload API fails due to network issue or permission denied
Then the system should stop upload process
And show toast message “Failed to upload file to storage. Please try again.”
test_cases.acceptance:
The system should stop upload process
The behavior should be validated when the storage upload API fails due to network issue or permission denied.

test_cases.summary:
Verify system provides retry option after upload failure
when the upload failed and error toast is shown
test_cases.description:
Feature: Storage Upload Failure – Retry Option Available

Scenario: Verify system provides retry option after upload failure

Given the upload failed and error toast is shown
When the user clicks Retry button (if available)
Then the system should attempt upload again
And should not crash or freeze
test_cases.acceptance:
The system should attempt upload again
The behavior should be validated when the user clicks Retry button (if available).

test_cases.summary:

when the user is in the JSON Upload dialog

test_cases.summary:

when FileReader fails during upload

Then the message should be readable and non-technical
And should not show stack trace or browser exception text
test_cases.acceptance:

The behavior should be validated when the system displays the toast.

test_cases.summary:
Verify system blocks upload when JSON contains deprecated field labelIds
when the user selects a valid JSON file for upload

Then the system should reject the file
And show toast message File "[filename]": "labelIds". Please provide labels as "labels": [{ "id": "" }].

test_cases.summary:
Verify schema error message includes filename and correction guidance
when the user uploads a JSON containing labelIds

When validation fails
Then the toast should include the filename
And should clearly instruct to use labels object array instead
test_cases.acceptance:
The toast should include the filename
The behavior should be validated when validation fails.

The behavior should be validated when the JSON contains a taxonomy annotation type that requires childAnnotation.

test_cases.acceptance:
The toast message should mention the specific annotationId causing the failure
The behavior should be validated when one annotation is missing childAnnotation.
